title: Agent loop termination
prompt: After Claude requests `lookup_order`, the application executes the tool. What should it do next?

options.A: End the loop because a tool has already produced the requested data
options.B: Append the tool result to conversation history and call Claude again
options.C: Search Claude's text for words such as “complete” before deciding
options.D: Start a new conversation containing only the tool result

explanation: `tool_use` means the application should execute the requested tool, append its result to the conversation, and let Claude decide the next action. Finish on `end_turn`, not after the first tool call and not by parsing prose.

title: Mandatory identity verification
prompt: Production logs show that refunds occasionally occur before identity verification, despite strong prompt instructions and examples. What is the most reliable correction?

options.A: Add more verification examples to the prompt
options.B: Ask Claude to state its confidence before refunding
options.C: Programmatically block refund calls until verified customer data exists
options.D: Cap the agent loop at five iterations

explanation: Identity verification before a financial action is a deterministic business requirement. Enforce it programmatically. Prompts and examples reduce failures but do not eliminate them.

title: Multi-concern request
prompt: A customer asks about two unrelated orders and also requests a human because the published policy does not cover one unusual item. What should the coordinator do?

options.A: Process every concern autonomously because the tools are available
options.B: Investigate both orders sequentially and escalate only if a tool fails
options.C: Decompose the concerns, gather relevant facts in parallel, and create a structured human handoff for the policy gap
options.D: Escalate without gathering any information because one concern is ambiguous

explanation: The system should preserve progress on solvable concerns while escalating the policy gap. Parallel investigation reduces latency, and a structured handoff gives the human the facts and recommended next actions.

title: Subagent context
prompt: A synthesis subagent produces unsupported conclusions even though the search subagent found strong evidence. Logs show the coordinator told synthesis only, “write the final report”. What is the root cause?

options.A: Synthesis needs every search tool as well
options.B: Subagents do not automatically inherit the coordinator's or other subagents' context
options.C: The system needs a larger model
options.D: Search and synthesis must always run in the same agent

explanation: Subagents have isolated contexts. The coordinator must explicitly pass search findings, evidence and attribution into the synthesis task.

title: Parallel research
prompt: Three independent source categories must be searched. Which coordinator behaviour gives true parallelism?

options.A: Emit all three `Task` tool calls in one coordinator response
options.B: Emit one `Task` call, wait for it, then emit the next
options.C: Give the coordinator Bash access and start background shell jobs
options.D: Use three named resumed sessions

explanation: Multiple `Task` calls emitted in one coordinator response can execute concurrently. Separate turns serialize the work.

title: Wrong tool selection
prompt: Claude repeatedly confuses `find_customer` and `find_order`. Both descriptions are one sentence and both accept a string identifier. What is the best first action?

options.A: Add a keyword router in front of Claude
options.B: Expand both descriptions with accepted inputs, examples, boundaries and when to use one rather than the other
options.C: Force `find_customer` on every request
options.D: Combine every backend operation into one general-purpose tool

explanation: Descriptions are Claude's primary tool-selection signal. Clarify purpose, input formats, examples and boundaries before adding a routing layer or merging distinct operations.

title: Actionable MCP errors
prompt: Which two responses best help an agent recover intelligently?

options.A: `{ "isError": true, "errorCategory": "transient", "isRetryable": true, "message": "CRM timed out" }`
options.B: `{ "result": [] }` after a timeout, reported as success
options.C: `{ "isError": true, "errorCategory": "permission", "isRetryable": false, "message": "User lacks refund permission" }`
options.D: `{ "error": "Operation failed" }` for every failure type

explanation: Both identify the failure category, whether retry is sensible, and a usable explanation. Empty success silently hides a timeout; a generic error prevents intelligent recovery.

title: Tool overload
prompt: A document-analysis subagent has 18 tools, including deployment, web publishing, CRM and financial tools it never needs. Selection accuracy has fallen. What should change?

options.A: Increase the number of few-shot examples while retaining all tools
options.B: Restrict it to the four or five tools required for document analysis
options.C: Force one general tool on every turn
options.D: Move all tool descriptions into the user prompt

explanation: Least privilege improves tool choice and safety. Agents should receive only the tools required for their role, with narrowly scoped exceptions for frequent cross-role needs.

title: Shared MCP configuration
prompt: A GitHub MCP server must be available to every developer who clones the project, while keeping its token out of source control. Which setup is correct?

options.A: Put the server and literal token in `CLAUDE.md`
options.B: Put the server in each user's `~/.claude.json`
options.C: Put the server in project `.mcp.json` and reference an environment variable for the token
options.D: Put the server in `.claude/commands/` and prompt for the token each time

explanation: Project `.mcp.json` is shared through version control. Environment-variable expansion keeps credentials out of the repository. User-level configuration is personal, not team-wide.

title: Shared command
prompt: The team wants `/security-review` to be version-controlled and available to every developer. Where should its command file live?

options.A: `~/.claude/commands/`
options.B: `.claude/commands/` in the repository
options.C: `.claude/rules/`
options.D: `.mcp.json`

explanation: Repository `.claude/commands/` is project-scoped and shared. `~/.claude/commands/` is personal.

title: Conditional conventions
prompt: All `*.test.tsx` files must follow one convention even though tests sit in many directories. What is the most maintainable configuration?

options.A: A user-level `CLAUDE.md`
options.B: One skill developers must remember to invoke
options.C: A `.claude/rules/` file with a `**/*.test.tsx` path glob
options.D: Duplicate `CLAUDE.md` files beside every test

explanation: Path-scoped rules apply automatically to matching files regardless of directory. They avoid duplication and do not depend on a developer remembering to invoke a skill.

title: Plan or execute
prompt: Which task is the clearest candidate for direct execution rather than plan mode?

options.A: Split a monolith into five services
options.B: Migrate an authentication library across 48 files
options.C: Choose between two event-driven architectures
options.D: Add a missing null check to one function with a clear failing test

explanation: A known, single-file fix with a failing test is appropriately bounded for direct execution. The other tasks involve architecture, broad dependencies or many files and should begin in plan mode.

title: Claude Code in CI
prompt: Which two options are appropriate for a non-interactive pipeline that posts machine-readable review findings?

options.A: Run Claude Code with `-p` or `--print`
options.B: Set the undocumented environment variable `CLAUDE_HEADLESS=true`
options.C: Use `--output-format json` with `--json-schema`
options.D: Resume the same session that generated the code so it remembers its reasoning

explanation: `-p`/`--print` prevents the command waiting for interactive input. JSON output plus a schema makes results machine-readable. The generator's session should not review its own work; use an independent instance.

title: False positives
prompt: A review agent flags harmless comments as defects. “Be conservative” and “report only high-confidence findings” have not helped. What should you try first?

options.A: Add explicit categorical criteria showing what constitutes a contradiction and what should be ignored
options.B: Increase the context window
options.C: Trust the agent's self-reported confidence
options.D: Run the same prompt three times and keep majority findings

explanation: Concrete reporting and exclusion criteria improve precision. Vague confidence language is poorly calibrated and does not define the actual decision boundary.

title: Guaranteed JSON shape
prompt: A downstream service must always receive syntactically schema-compliant output. Which method is most reliable?

options.A: Ask Claude to return JSON in a fenced code block
options.B: Provide one JSON example and parse the text
options.C: Define a tool with the required JSON schema and force that tool selection
options.D: Retry any malformed text without telling Claude what failed

explanation: Tool use with a JSON schema is the most reliable way to guarantee syntactically compliant structure. It does not guarantee semantic correctness, so validation is still required.

title: Missing source fields
prompt: Some invoices legitimately omit a purchase-order number. The current schema requires one, and the model sometimes invents it. What should change?

options.A: Add “do not hallucinate” to the prompt but retain the required field
options.B: Make the field optional or nullable and validate downstream rules separately
options.C: Replace the schema with free text
options.D: Retry until two runs agree

explanation: If information may be absent, the schema must represent absence. Making a field mandatory pressures the model to fabricate. Business constraints belong in separate validation.

title: Batch processing
prompt: Which workload is the best fit for the Message Batches API?

options.A: A blocking security check required before every merge
options.B: An interactive customer-support conversation
options.C: An overnight audit of 20,000 archived documents needed the following afternoon
options.D: An agent loop that must call a tool and return its result several times in one request

explanation: Batch processing offers cost savings but may take up to 24 hours and has no latency guarantee. That is suitable for a large, non-blocking overnight audit—not interactive or blocking work, and not a multi-turn tool loop inside one batch request.

title: Long support conversations
prompt: A 40-turn case contains exact refund amounts and order IDs, while MCP tools return dozens of irrelevant fields. Which two changes best preserve reliability?

options.A: Maintain a structured case-facts block with exact IDs, amounts, dates and statuses
options.B: Keep every raw tool response in full because more context is always safer
options.C: Trim tool results to fields relevant to the case before appending them
options.D: Repeatedly summarise the whole conversation into a single paragraph

explanation: Preserve exact transactional facts outside lossy summaries, and stop irrelevant tool fields consuming context. More raw context is not automatically better.

title: Escalation
prompt: A customer explicitly says, “I want to speak to a human now.” The issue itself appears straightforward. What should the agent do?

options.A: Try to solve it first because escalation is expensive
options.B: Ask the customer to rate their frustration
options.C: Honour the explicit request and escalate immediately with a useful handoff
options.D: Use a self-confidence threshold to decide

explanation: An explicit request for a human is itself an escalation trigger. The agent should honour it and provide a structured handoff rather than using sentiment or model confidence.

title: Conflicting sources
prompt: Two credible reports give different market-size figures and were collected in different years. What should the synthesis pipeline do?

options.A: Select the newer figure and omit the older one
options.B: Average the figures
options.C: Preserve both values with source attribution, dates and methodological context, and mark the disagreement
options.D: Ask the model which figure feels more plausible

explanation: Credible conflicts should remain visible. Dates and methods may explain the difference. Preserve claim-source mappings and let readers understand what is established versus contested.
